Fair enough. I view it somewhat like the OK sign being appropriated by 4chan. The OK sign does not traditionally mean White power, and generally it's best to ignore SJWs as there is no way to appease them and attempting to do so would only make it impossible to have a functional society. Having said that, I'm not a fan of starting fights, or doing things to cause disruption. If a company or institution wants to set policies for its members to follow that should be up to them. It's reasonable to tell people not to do something which although innocuous in itself, insights certain people to go unhinged and cause problems (I'm talking about this in the context of what happens on the job, not what people do on their own time). But there's a slippery slope. While telling people not to do things that don't need to be done, and which they'd only do to provoke their adversaries, is perfectly reasonable; if you tell people to refrain from something they should be doing or would normally do, only to appease a belligerent group, you're not preventing disruption, you're just going along with their disruption.

If a school can't teach classic literature, show classic plays, or educate their students as they should, then the school has already failed. If they choose not to because some people are offended, then they are simply choosing not to do their job. As far as lawsuits go, you absolutely should not be able to sue any person, company or institution in America for exorcising rights explicitly recognized in the First Amendment (although the option should exist to vote on changing public leadership).
